correctness.rationale: With induced area density (1+(r/R) cos(theta))/(2pi), exact one-point tensor moments imply m2=2(R²+2r²), m4=(12R⁴+52R²r²+39r⁴)/2, m6=(40R⁶+312R⁴r²+516R²r⁴+187r⁶)/2. Their normalized fourth derivative is (2-13x)/(4(1+2x)^3), proving the full range and exactly-two ambiguity interval. Cross-multiplying two fourth ratios yields the partner involution y=(4-9x)/(52x+9). J-6K has derivative 3(51x²+8)/(16(1+2x)^4); its strictly decreasing derivative has infimum 59/432 at x=1, proving uniqueness and optimal inverse coefficient. The unsquared-ratio exponent 1/2 is optimal as x approaches zero. A direct independent angular quadrature for 10 parameter pairs, exact polynomial identities, an explicit rational collision and inverse checks were executed from the included verifier and passed. Finite computations are diagnostics, not replacements for the proof.

originality.rationale: A surface-area sampled Euclidean embedded ring torus is distinct from the sphere, spherical-volume, flat-torus, cylinder and polygon settings in accessible prior sources. The central retained claim is the exact two-to-one inverse classification plus the sharp globally stable three-consecutive-even-moment inverse, not the general existence of moment formulas or convolution identities. The inspected primary literature describes forward distance laws or generic shape-moment methods and does not state or logically imply the exact torus partner involution, multiplicity interval or sharp inverse coefficient. This is a best-knowledge assessment; historical priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: Bounded searches cannot exclude an unindexed, unpublished or differently named prior inverse ring-torus theorem.
The Gallatin source was scrutinized through the relevant early pages and scope, not through a line-by-line entire-manuscript priority adjudication.
The general compact-set convolution approach might permit derivations of the moment polynomials; forward integration is not claimed as the essential novelty.
The theorem uses exact population moments and does not establish finite-sample stability.

value.rationale: The precise fibers of two Euclidean chord moments for a standard embedded genus-one surface form a natural geometric inverse problem. Rather than just computing low moments, the theorem identifies an exact open two-to-one ambiguity interval, a rational partner involution, an explicit noncongruent equal-moment example, the minimal number of consecutive even moments needed for global reconstruction, and a sharp global Lipschitz coefficient for a stable aspect-ratio observable. The result supplies a mathematically motivated identifiability boundary for geometric measurement and is not merely an arbitrary numerical slice.
